title: Separatedness descends along surjective universally closed morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $p:X\to S$ and $q:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism with $q\circ f=p$. Assume $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If $p$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] (the diagonal $X\to X\times_SX$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]), then $q$ is separated.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 09MQ (lemma-image-universally-closed-separated), part (4), and its proof (last paragraph: $X\to Y\times_SY$ closed as a composition of closed maps, $X\to Y$ surjective, so $\Delta_{Y/S}(Y)$ is closed; separated by the discussion after Schemes, Definition 01KK)

proof.text: Write $\Delta_X:X\to X\times_SX$ and $\Delta_Y:Y\to Y\times_SY$ for the diagonals of $p$ and $q$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $f\times_Sf:X\times_SX\to Y\times_SY$ for the induced morphism of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $(f\times_Sf)\circ\Delta_X=\Delta_Y\circ f$: both are morphisms $X\to Y\times_SY$ whose two components (compositions with the projections) are $f$, so they agree by the uniqueness in the universal property of $Y\times_SY$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 09MQ (lemma-image-universally-closed-separated), proof, the commutative square $X\to X\times_SX\to Y\times_SY$, $X\to Y\to Y\times_SY$

proof.text: The morphism $f\times_Sf$ is universally closed [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-product-map], applied with $f_1=f_2=f$ (a morphism over $S$ since $q\circ f=p$). In particular it is a closed map of underlying spaces: by the definition of universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], its base change along $\mathrm{id}_{Y\times_SY}$, which is $f\times_Sf$ itself, is closed.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 09MQ (lemma-image-universally-closed-separated), proof, first paragraph ('The right vertical arrow is universally closed as a composition of the universally closed morphisms $X\times_SX\to X\times_SY\to Y\times_SY$')

proof.text: Since $p$ is separated, $\Delta_X$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence a homeomorphism onto a closed subset of $X\times_SX$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and so a closed map of underlying spaces. By Step 2 the composite $(f\times_Sf)\circ\Delta_X$ is a composition of closed maps, hence closed; in particular its image $(f\times_Sf)(\Delta_X(X))$ is closed in $Y\times_SY$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 09MQ (lemma-image-universally-closed-separated), proof, last paragraph ('Then $X\to Y\times_SY$ is closed as a composition of closed morphisms')

proof.text: By Step 1 this image equals $\Delta_Y(f(X))$, and $f(X)=Y$ because $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Hence $\Delta_Y(Y)$ is a closed subset of $Y\times_SY$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 09MQ (lemma-image-universally-closed-separated), proof, last paragraph ('Since $X\to Y$ is surjective, it follows that $\Delta_{Y/S}(Y)$ is closed in $Y\times_SY$')

proof.text: The diagonal $\Delta_Y$ is an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-diagonal-immersion], and by Step 4 its image is closed, so $\Delta_Y$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion]. Hence $q$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism].
